title: Controlling Biology - Fabian Theis, Helmholtz Munich
author: RJ Honicky
description: As systems biology efforts heat up to map biology at higher resolution, greater breadth and more modalities, Fabian Theis is pushing the frontier from mapping to predicting to controlling biology
summary: Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”multiomics”), time-varying biological data.
takeaways: After a lot of initial excitement, Virtual Cell projects have received less attention, due in no small part to questions about the effectiveness of large-scale models in solving even basic Virtual Cell problems.
Virtual cells struggle This kind of multi-scale, multi-modal data looks a lot like the data Fabian has made a career out modeling.

The 2025 Arc Virtual Cell Challenge shined a light on the problem: a slew of papers pointed out that constant baselines (not even linear!) often beat sophisticated models for “Perturbation Prediction”.
